passage: Come here, Tuku, and put the phone down a minute. I am Kalyani, your Thakuma, and this is about your Dadu. When I was twenty, Arnab was a boy from the next department who wrote me shy notes. One day he asked, all light-hearted, whether we could swap private photos on our phones. "Everyone does it," he said. I did not want to. I went quiet and hoped he would read it from my face. He did not; he was only waiting for my answer. That night my stomach hurt. Next morning I said it plainly: "Arnab, I am not comfortable with that. I like meeting and talking." His ears went red. He said sorry and never asked again. Say plainly what suits you, Tuku, and expect to be heard.

qa.q: What did Arnab ask Kalyani for?
qa.a: He asked whether they could swap private photos on their phones.

qa.q: What did Kalyani hope when she went quiet, and what does her stomach ache that night suggest?
qa.a: She hoped Arnab would understand from her face. The stomach ache suggests she was uneasy and did not know how to say no.

qa.q: What did Kalyani do the next morning, and why did it help?
qa.a: She told Arnab plainly that she was not comfortable and that she liked meeting and talking. Clear words left him nothing to guess.

qa.q: How might Arnab have seen her silence that day?
qa.a: He was only waiting for an answer, so he probably did not realise she was uncomfortable until she spoke. Once she did, he said sorry and never asked again.

grounding: An elder recalls being unsure about sharing photos, hoping to be guessed, then saying plainly what she was comfortable with.

passage:
Late on Sunday, Jomon's phone buzzed in the middle of revision.
Sarita: miss you. send me a shirtless pic? just for me
Jomon: haha
Jomon: ok actually, not joking now. i'm not comfortable sending pics like that
Jomon: not to anyone, not just you
Sarita: oh. i didn't mean anything bad
Jomon: i know. i just didn't want to send one and then feel weird about it all week
Jomon: selfies in the canteen, totally fine. anything without a shirt, no
Sarita: got it. thanks for telling me straight
Sarita: honestly i'd rather know than guess
Jomon: same here. if something's not ok for you, say it too
Sarita: deal. call at 10?
Jomon: yes. i'll even wear the shirt
Sarita: lol ok

qa.q: What did Sarita ask Jomon to send?
Why did Jomon type "haha" first and then "not joking now"?
qa.a: Jomon felt awkward and was tempted to laugh it off, but wanted to be honest rather than send a photo and feel uneasy about it all week.

qa.q: What made Jomon's reply a clear boundary?
qa.a: It named exactly what was fine (canteen selfies) and what wasn't, without blaming Sarita, and invited Sarita to state limits too.

qa.q: How does Sarita take Jomon's honesty?
qa.a: Sarita is thankful to be told straight and says it's better to know than to guess, then makes an easy plan for a call at 10.

grounding: Shows feeling unsure about sharing photos and saying plainly what one is comfortable with instead of going along to avoid awkwardness.

passage:
At the Dussehra fair in Rampur, Farhan and Sharmila had slipped away from their friends to the quiet side of the ghat, behind the balloon sellers. They had been together four months. Sharmila leaned her head on his shoulder. "Nobody's around. We could go further down, near the boats."
Farhan's stomach tightened. Part of him wanted to just nod along and hope she'd read his silence. Instead he said, "Can I tell you something a bit awkward?"
"Always."
"I like this. Holding hands, sitting close. I'm not ready for more than that yet. I didn't want to say yes just to skip an uncomfortable moment."
Sharmila was quiet, then squeezed his hand. "I'm glad you told me instead of going along." She pointed at the giant wheel, lit up against the sky. "That, then?"
They walked back into the noise, fingers laced.

qa.q: How long had Farhan and Sharmila been together?
What did Farhan feel when Sharmila suggested going near the boats?
qa.a: His stomach tightened; he felt uneasy and was tempted to nod along and hope she would read his silence.

qa.q: What did Farhan say, and why did it work?
qa.a: That he liked holding hands and sitting close but wasn't ready for more; saying it plainly let Sharmila respect it instead of guessing.

qa.q: How might Sharmila have seen the moment?
qa.a: Surprised for a second, then trusting and glad he was honest, which she shows by squeezing his hand and suggesting the giant wheel.

grounding: Illustrates being unsure about physical closeness and stating one's comfort plainly instead of hoping a partner will guess.
